{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_vrtx_011CgTfKmx58GtuHFDuPtXhB","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Both scenarios are fixed. Focus now lands on a toolbar button in A4 and B3, and the earlier frames behave as before.\n\n**Cause:** a toolbar item could only receive Tab focus if it was the active item. When the active item couldn't take focus, every button in the toolbar was skipped by Tab:\n- **A:** Italic was active and then removed by \"Toggle Italic\", so Shift+Tab jumped to \"Before\".\n- **B:** the active item was the disabled Bold, so Tab went from \"Before\" straight to \"After\". This happens when the starting active item is set to a disabled button; with no starting item set, it already worked.\n\n**Fix:** the change is in `packages/ariakit-react-core/src/composite/composite-item.tsx`. If the active item is missing or disabled, the first enabled item becomes the one Tab can reach. Only that one button is added, so:\n- **A4:** Shift+Tab focuses Bold, as in Expected A. Pressing Shift+Tab again goes to \"Before\".\n- **B3:** Tab focuses Italic, as in Expected B. Pressing Tab again goes to \"After\".\n- Focusing that button makes it the active item again, so arrow keys work as usual afterwards.\n- When the active item is valid, nothing changes.\n\n**Testing:** I rebuilt both scenarios as temporary tests. Pressing Shift+Tab again goes to \"Before\".\n- **B3:** Tab focuses Italic, as in Expected B.
